evidence_cards.content: Amazon Payments and PayPal customers with a history of non-payment (orders cancelled after 7 days) are subjected to an escalation process if they fail to pay for auction winnings more than three times in a twelve-month period, unless three times is less than 10% of their total winnings.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a threshold-based exception flow (escalation policy) triggered by repeated non-payment (>3 times in 12 months OR >10% win rate unpaid), which imposes additional restrictions beyond simple account locking.

evidence_cards.content: Example #1: If Customer A wins 11 auctions in 12 months and has 4 unpaid orders (after item #12 goes unpaid), she becomes subject to the escalation policy — demonstrating that exceeding 3 unpaid orders triggers escalation regardless of percentage.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Provides concrete evidence of the exception flow trigger: 4th unpaid order in 12 months → escalation policy applied, even if under 10% threshold (4/12 = 33%).

evidence_cards.content: Example #2: Customer B wins 55 auctions in 12 months with 5 unpaid (9%) — not yet escalated; but if she fails to pay for a 56th auction (6 unpaid, 10.7%), she becomes subject to escalation — showing that crossing the 10% threshold triggers escalation even if under 3 occurrences.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Demonstrates the alternative trigger condition for escalation: exceeding 10% unpaid rate (even if <3 occurrences) activates the exception flow, requiring CS Rep intervention per occurrence until rate falls below 10%.
